prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: Thanks to  employee for getting me off the standby list and assigning me a seat!
Delta: On behalf of *TMA, you are most welcome. Just an FYI, with a Basic Economy ticket, when you see yourself on "Stand-by", it refers only to the seat assignment. You are confirmed for the flight. It just means you're waiting for a seat assignment. *TAC

Customer: says I'm on "standby" but I bought a ticket. Should I be concerned? #help
Delta: You're on standby for a seat assignment, no need to worry. *AJY

Customer: Hi, your phone system has hung up on me twice. Now it says wait time is over 45m. My wife & I are on a flight tomorrow but booked separately. Just checked in to select seats together and it says we can’t because we’re on standby list?!? We booked months ago. Please help.
Delta: Hello! I am here to help. Could you provide both confirmation numbers via DM so I can take a look for you? Thanks. *TDL https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Customer: Still don't have a seat assignment for my flight.   please don't let me down. #flying #nervous
Delta: Hello! Please Dm your confirmation# and I will try to assist. *TCC

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: general_question):
"""I have a question about a reservation that says I'm on the Standby List. Why don't I have a seat?"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: You're on standby for a seat assignment, not a confirmed seat yet. Please DM us your confirmation number so we can look into it for you.
